label: prf:commutative-chirality-vanishes
title: Proof of commutative chirality vanishes
html:
Proof. By Frobenius S-classification, h_{\mathrm{A}} = q - q^{-1} has S-eigenvalue -1, so h_{\mathrm{A}}^2 has eigenvalue +1. As q \to 1, h_{\mathrm{A}} \to 0 continuously, hence h_{\mathrm{A}}^2 \to 0. The chirality functional \Phi_3 = \sum_i \log\lvert\chi^{\mathrm{sym}}_i / \chi^{\mathrm{alt}}_i\rvert remains finite (each per-factor ratio approaches \pm 1 classically; the sum of logs approaches 0 for any chain whose primitive factors include at least one ud crossing, and it approaches a finite limit otherwise). The product h_{\mathrm{A}}^2 \Phi_3 \to 0 \cdot \Phi_3 = 0.

For the quantum 3-integer: \lim_{q \to 1}[3]_q = \lim_{q \to 1}(q^2 + 1 + q^{-2}) = 3. \square

Companion reading. The crossing-energy interpretation of the commutative limit (commutative crossing energy) shows that the same vanishing h_{\mathrm{A}} \to 0 corresponds geometrically to the unit-circle parameterisation q = e^{i\varTheta}, where the crossing weight q - q^{-1} = 2i\sin\varTheta becomes pure imaginary. The two readings agree: the chirality channel collapses to zero in the strict commutative limit, while a unit-circle deformation recovers a non-trivial \mathrm{U}(1) phase.

Diagnostic application. The commutative limit provides a structural test: any feature of the formula that persists as q \to 1 is independent of the quantum deformation and lies in the underlying classical representation theory. canonical scan (the formal derivation) confirms that the proton--neutron mass splitting vanishes in the strict q \to 1 limit (consistent with the chirality channel being the unique S-odd carrier), and that the wrong-sign binding for Z = N fully-paired atoms (D, {}^{4}\mathrm{He}) is not a q-deformation artefact but a structural feature of \Phi_1 in the symmetric group algebra \mathbb{C}[S_n] = H_n(1).
